# Slope gives velocity

<!-- STEP id="triangle" -->
Take two points on the vehicle's line: A at (2 s, 40 m) and B at (4 s, 80 m). Draw the triangle ABC. BC is the change in position, 40 m. CA is the change in time, 2 s.

<!-- STEP id="slope" -->
Velocity = BC / CA = 40 m / 2 s = 20 m/s. BC / CA is the **slope** of the line, its steepness.

**The slope of a position-time graph gives the velocity.**

<!-- STEP id="compare" -->
Back to A and B. In the same time interval, B's displacement is larger. So B's line is steeper, and B's velocity is higher.
